title: Built for the Burn: Your 7-Day Training Plan
excerpt: Strength. Sweat. Recovery. Repeat. Four structured workouts, one optional movement day and two days to recover.
author: IGNYTE Active
cover_alt: IGNYTE athlete training in the gym

body.text: You don't have to train every day to make progress. You need a plan that challenges you, gives your body time to recover and fits into your life.
Whether you're building strength, improving your fitness or getting back into a consistent routine, this weekly training plan is designed to keep you moving with purpose.
Four structured workouts. One optional movement day. Two days to recover.
No complicated routines. No unnecessary exercises. Just a balanced week of training you can make your own.
Ready to bring the fire?
YOUR WEEK AT A GLANCE_
These times are approximate. Adjust the exercises, weights and intensity to suit your experience and fitness level.
MONDAY_
Lower Body. Strong Foundations.
Start the week by building strength through your legs, glutes and core.
THE WORKOUT
Rest for 60–90 seconds between sets.
Choose weights that make the final few repetitions challenging while allowing you to maintain good technique.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Controlled movement, consistent effort and building strength from the ground up.
TUESDAY_
Upper Body. Find Your Strength.
Today is about building upper body strength while keeping your core engaged.
THE WORKOUT

rows: Lat Pulldowns or Resistance Band Pulldowns

body.text: Rest for 60–90 seconds between sets.
Modify push-ups using an elevated surface or your knees if needed.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Strength, stability and controlled movement.
WEDNESDAY_
Active Recovery. Keep Moving.
Recovery isn't time wasted. It's part of the process.
Today, swap intense training for gentle movement that helps you feel refreshed.
CHOOSE YOUR MOVEMENT

A 20–30 minute walk
Gentle yoga or Pilates
Light cycling
A mobility and stretching session
Keep the intensity comfortable. You should be able to hold a conversation throughout.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Move without pushing. Give your body an opportunity to recover before the next session.
THURSDAY_
HIIT. Bring the Fire.
Time to turn up the intensity.
High Intensity Interval Training alternates challenging efforts with periods of recovery.
You don't need an hour. You need a focused session that matches your fitness level.
THE WORKOUT
Start with a five-minute warm-up.
Choose a stationary bike, rowing machine, brisk incline walk or running intervals.
Complete five rounds of:

60 seconds: Challenging effort
2 minutes: Easy recovery pace
Finish with a five-minute cool-down.
Aim for approximately 7–8 out of 10 effort during the hard intervals. Challenging, but controlled. If you're new to interval training, start with three rounds at a moderate intensity.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Build cardiovascular fitness and practise recovering between efforts.
FRIDAY_
Full Body. Finish Strong.
Bring everything together with a full body workout that combines strength, balance and control.
THE WORKOUT
Rest for 60–90 seconds between sets.
Focus on movement quality rather than rushing through the workout.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Total body strength and finishing the training week with intention.
SATURDAY_
Your Move. Your Rules.
Today is optional.
Choose something you enjoy, whether that means pushing your fitness a little further or simply moving for the fun of it.
OPTION A: COMBAT & CONDITIONING
Try six rounds of:

2 minutes of shadowboxing or bag work
1 minute of easy recovery
Keep your combinations controlled, especially if you're new to boxing.
OPTION B: STEADY CARDIO
Spend 30–45 minutes walking, cycling, swimming or jogging at a comfortable pace.
OPTION C: TAKE AN EXTRA REST DAY
If you're feeling fatigued or need more recovery, take it.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Consistency without forcing intensity.
SUNDAY_
Rest. Reset. Come Back Stronger.
No structured training required.
Take the day to recharge, get adequate sleep and prepare for the week ahead.
Progress isn't just about how hard you train. It's also about giving yourself enough time to adapt.

body.label: THE FOCUS_
body.text: Recover well and get ready to move again.
MAKE THE PLAN YOUR OWN_
There isn't one perfect way to train. The best routine is the one you can follow consistently.
If you're just getting started
Start with two sets per strength exercise, use lighter weights and reduce the number of HIIT intervals. You can also spread the four structured sessions across more than seven days.
If you're more experienced
Increase your weights gradually, add a set where appropriate or increase interval difficulty as your fitness improves. Progress doesn't have to mean making every workout harder.
If life gets busy
Prioritise the sessions you can realistically fit in. Three consistent workouts are more useful than an ambitious seven-day routine you can't maintain.
Before every workout
Allow approximately five minutes to warm up with gentle cardio and movements relevant to the session. Finish with a few minutes of easier movement.
If you're injured, returning after a long break or managing a medical condition, get appropriate individual advice before beginning.
BUILT FOR THE BURN_
Find Your Fit. Bring Your Fire.
How you move is personal. What you wear should support that.
Whether you're lifting, stretching, running or powering through your next HIIT session, choose gear that feels comfortable, stays in place and suits the demands of your workout.
